sourceEvidence.claim: THE THREE RULES, verbatim — (1) pelvic splanchnic nerves and CNs III, VII, IX, and X are part of the parasympathetic nervous system; (2) adrenal medulla is directly innervated by preganglionic sympathetic fibers; (3) sweat glands are part of the sympathetic pathway but are innervated by cholinergic fibers (sympathetic nervous system results in a “chold” sweat — the source's OWN TYPO, carried verbatim)

kypExtensions.summary: The ganglionic-blocker miniCase — a man on an Nn-blocker infusion (trimethaphan) for aortic-dissection hypertension, asked which synaptic transmission remains fully intact; the correct answer is the somatic NMJ (Nm), with four distractors built from the page's own wiring rules (adrenal medulla 'postganglionic' misread, vascular NE 'downstream' misread, sweat-gland cholinergic-vs-nicotinic conflation, bowel M3 location-vs-traffic conflation).
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid prints the wiring figure and the three rules but never integrates them into a what-survives-ganglionic-blockade vignette; the trimethaphan stem, the warm-dry-skin/ileus/retention findings, and all four distractor mechanisms are KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The five-gate reading protocol (WHICH COLUMN → WHICH FIBER IS LONG → WHICH TRANSMITTER → WHICH RECEPTOR CHIP → WHICH EXCEPTION) and the ganglionic-blocker reasoning callout (what Nn blockade silences vs spares) — KYP's synthesis of the wiring figure, its transmitter stamps, and its three rules into one protocol.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the figure and the rules but no reading order; the five-gate protocol, the Nn-blockade silences/spares ledger, and the length-rule framing are KYP's design.
